title: The Boatwright
logline: In a lagoon-side yard, a boatbuilder lashes eight separate timbers into one outrigger hull, testing each binding before trusting the whole craft to open water.
human_question: What holds a group of separate, ordinary parts together well enough to carry someone across open water?

premise.story: A boatbuilder constructs or repairs a traditional lashed or outrigger fishing craft, timber by timber, binding by binding, through to its first launch.
premise.experience: The physical logic of a vessel that only becomes seaworthy once every one of its separate parts is properly bound to the others.

concept_links.why: The source compares the eight path factors to a raft of eight great logs, bound together, that carries a person across the ocean to the far shore [C076-P:L1413]. The film gives that comparison a real, physical form without ever stating it.
The eightfold path is what makes up the path minds this group's other films also touch; the boatbuilder's craft is one more honest, physical echo of 'carrying across.'

what_camera_could_observe: Individual timbers selected, shaped and tested
The lashing and binding process, and a loose binding being retested and corrected
The completed hull checked for balance before launch
The first launch through the surf or into the lagoon
what_must_be_real: A real, working boatbuilder's actual commission or repair. No boat is built solely for the film if it will not actually be used.

possible_arc.turn: A binding tested and found wanting, redone.
possible_arc.ending_open: The finished boat's first launch, and whether it performs as intended.

requirements: A boatyard where traditional lashed or outrigger construction is still practised
A real commission or repair during the filming window

suggestions.name: Negombo lagoon
suggestions.why: A well-known centre for traditional outrigger fishing craft.
suggestions.verify: Whether lashed (rather than nailed or fibreglass) construction is still practised there must be confirmed.

risks: Traditional lashed construction may be rare or no longer practised; do not stage a revival for the film
Romanticising a hard, often precarious livelihood
drop_if: No boatyard still builds or repairs craft this way, or none will allow filming of a real commission

connections.note: From one crossing to the boats and craft of a coastal community nearby.
From the boat that carries people across, to the community that lands and sells what the sea gives.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
